gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: 'We'd already booked when you called,' they said. They said they ___ already booked when I called.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; only the pronoun you → I shifts.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't leave your belongings unattended,' the announcement repeated. The announcement ___ passengers not to leave their belongings unattended.
gaps.hint: warn sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: The warning fits warn + object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.

gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: "We are leaving now." — They said they ___ then.
